name: Technology and cyber
purpose: information security, phishing, passwords and MFA, data handling, physical security and tailgating, incident response, AI literacy, secure software practices

identity.place: The technology centre of a national home-and-garden retailer (about 400 people in technology): a two-storey 2016 concrete-framed building on a business park at the edge of an inland city, clad in dark grey fibre-cement panels with long horizontal windows. The ground floor holds the company's own data hall (about 40 racks), entered only through a security vestibule off the main corridor. The first floor holds the engineering floor, the security operations centre (SOC) and the incident room.
architecture: long horizontal ribbon windows on the outer walls: sill at 0.9 m, head at 2.7 m, slim black aluminium frames with mullions every 1.35 m and no transoms; pale grey roller blinds; the data hall has no windows at all

the first floor: round fair-faced concrete columns 0.4 m across on a 7.2 m grid; a flat concrete soffit painted white at 3.2 m with long black linear pendant lights, black wire cable baskets and a white sprinkler pipe; light grey carpet tiles
internal walls are white plasterboard; the company's colour is cobalt blue, used on one wall of each room, on doors into secure areas and on chair upholstery; felt acoustic panels in pale grey

glass partitions on the first floor have black frames and two frosted bands at 0.9 m and 1.5 m (plain, no words); the SOC and the incident room have solid walls to the corridor and a glass door with frosted glass

the data hall: a 0.6 m raised floor of 600 mm square grey steel tiles (perforated tiles in the cold aisles), white walls, black racks in rows, contained cold aisles with glass sliding doors at each end, overhead yellow fibre trays and black cable baskets, a white ceiling at 3.6 m above the floor with linear lights
secure doors: cobalt blue steel doors in grey steel frames, each with a card reader and a keypad at 1.1 m, a small black dome camera above, and a green push-to-exit button on the inside
identity.materials: white plasterboard and white-painted concrete, fair-faced grey concrete columns, light grey carpet tiles, black powder-coated steel (racks, frames, cable baskets), light oak veneer on desk tops, cobalt blue as the company's colour (one wall per room, secure doors, upholstery), pale grey felt, black screens; signal yellow only on fibre trays and floor tile lifters; signal red only on the few things that are red in life (a fire extinguisher, a fire alarm call point, the gas suppression release)
inhabited: screens everywhere, always as slots: code, alerts, dashboards and chat drawn by the engine, never by the set
engineers' things: noise-cancelling headphones on a monitor, a laptop on a stand, a mechanical keyboard, a stack of sticky notes (blank), a mug, a small plant, a rubber duck on a monitor base
security in plain sight: badges on lanyards, card readers and keypads by doors, a privacy filter on a laptop, a locked cabinet, a clear desk at night
infrastructure: floor boxes and cable baskets, a fire extinguisher by each door, a first-aid box, labels on racks as plain coloured strips (no words)
slight wear: a chair with one armrest lower, a scuffed kick plate on a secure door, cable ties left in a fibre tray
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; the first floor's soffit is at 3.2 m; a door is 2.1 m high and 0.9 m wide (secure doors 1.0 m wide)
desks are 1.6 by 0.8 m at 0.72 m (sit-stand, up to about 1.1 m); a monitor is a 27 inch screen about 0.61 by 0.36 m
a rack is 0.6 m wide, 1.2 m deep and 2.0 m high (42U) on a raised floor 0.6 m above the slab; a cold aisle is 1.8 m wide (three tiles) and a hot aisle 1.2 m (two tiles)
the SOC's video wall is eight 55 inch panels (each about 1.21 by 0.68 m) in a 4 by 2 array about 4.9 m wide and 1.37 m tall, its base at 1.2 m

a card reader sits at about 1.1 m beside a door; a fire extinguisher hangs with its handle about 1 m above the floor; green exit signs (a running figure and an arrow, no words) sit above exit doors at about 2.3 m
identity.default_light: Late morning on an overcast day: soft, even, cool daylight through the long ribbon windows on the first floor, and the neutral white linear lights on everywhere. In the data hall there is no daylight: even white light from the ceiling, the racks' small status LEDs (green and blue) and a slightly cool cast. Shadows are soft and short. Screens are on (their slots are lit).
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every scene so the sets belong to one place (each scene names the ones its camera can see): one cobalt blue element (a wall, a secure door, upholstery), a round fair-faced concrete column, the long black-framed ribbon window, a black cable basket or a yellow fibre tray, a card reader and keypad by a door, pale grey felt.
avoid: a hacker cliche: hooded figures, green code rain, skulls, padlock icons floating in the air, a dark room lit only by screens
exposed brick, small-paned steel factory windows, birch ply, brass lamps, deep green, marigold or burgundy (they belong to other places)
real brands, logos, operating system looks, signs with words, flags or anything that pins a country
people in the sets (the cast is separate)
words, numbers or real code on screens, labels or boards (empty slots only)
screens facing a window or with a window directly behind them: screens sit at about 90 degrees to the windows
a catalogue-clean tech office: every scene shows that people work here
identity.outside: Through the ribbon windows: the business park's car park with a few trees in planted islands, a low hedge, other low grey buildings without signs, and a flat overcast sky.

cast.role: software engineers and developers, varied in age, background and build
SOC analysts and the SOC shift lead
an incident manager and the people on the bridge (IT, legal, communications)

research: Real-space facts checked on 2026-10-15 (rack sizes: makers' and resellers' listings, sizes only; hot and cold aisles and perforated tiles: a hardware site-preparation guide; security vestibules, anti-tailgating and anti-passback: data centre security training and door hardware guides; SOC video walls and consoles: an integrator's case study, a government SOC specification and a practitioner forum). Sources and what was not verified: docs/research/2026-10-13-sets-tech_cyber.md.

objects.server rack: a black steel 42U cabinet 0.6 m wide, 1.2 m deep and 2.0 m high standing on the raised floor, bayed side by side in a row; a perforated mesh front door (fine round holes) in a slim frame with a vertical handle and a small lock; through the mesh, servers as thin horizontal bands with tiny green and blue status LEDs and black blanking panels in empty slots; plain coloured label strips (no words)
objects.containment: a cold aisle enclosure: clear glass roof panels in slim black aluminium frames laid across the aisle on the rack tops at about 2.1 to 2.2 m, and at each end a pair of bi-parting sliding glass doors 2.1 m high in black frames, with a black pull handle on each leaf and a brush seal at the floor

objects.linear pendant: a long slim black LED fitting about 1.8 m long hung on two fine wires from the soffit, its underside glowing evenly
objects.cable basket: a black wire mesh tray about 0.3 m wide hung from the soffit on threaded rods, carrying bundled cables
objects.desk phone: a low dark grey desk phone with a handset in its cradle, a coiled cord and a small slot screen; keys as plain squares
objects.headphones: over-ear headphones with a padded band and round ear cups, in black, hung on a small hook or laid on a desk
objects.mug: a cylinder with an elliptical rim in perspective and a handle loop; mismatched shapes

objects.kanban board: a large white board 2.0 by 1.0 m fixed to the wall, ruled into columns with thin black tape, with coloured square sticky notes in the columns (no words)

objects.sticky notes: a small stack of square paper notes, blank, one stuck to a monitor's edge
objects.network node: a rounded plinth like a short thick disc, 1.6 m across and 0.5 m high in the space's scale, pale grey with a cobalt ring around its top edge; on top, one large simple symbol, about 1.2 m across, shows what the node is: a server (a short black rack with LED dots), a laptop (open, its screen a slot), a phone (upright, its screen a slot) or a router (a flat box with two short aerials)
objects.link: a smooth cobalt blue tube about 0.15 m thick lying on the floor and curving gently between two nodes, like a cable drawn as a clean line; brighter where a packet is travelling
objects.data packet: a small rounded cube about 0.3 m on a side, pale with a cobalt edge and a tiny envelope mark on one face (no letters), sitting on a link; a closed padlock mark on its face when it is encrypted
objects.firewall: a freestanding translucent wall segment about 3 m long and 2.2 m high, made of stacked rounded pale bricks with soft cobalt joints, standing across a link with a single gate opening where the link passes
objects.cloud: a soft rounded white cloud form, about 4 m wide, floating above the far horizon on the right, with one link rising into it
objects.grid floor: a flat, pale floor with a faint square grid (lines every 1 m), receding to a soft horizon; no texture beyond the grid

scenes.what: a contained cold aisle in the company's data hall, seen from its open near end: two rows of black racks facing each other across perforated floor tiles under a clear glass roof, with glass sliding doors closing the far end
scenes.for: physical security on the data hall floor, escorting visitors, a technician replacing a drive, cooling explained, no photos and clean hands rules
plan: Seen from above, metres, heights from the raised floor's surface: x runs across the aisle (its centre line x 0); y runs along it from its near end (y 0) to its far end (y 7.2). The raised floor is 0.6 m above the slab; the hall's ceiling is 3.6 m above the floor.

The cold aisle is 1.8 m wide (three tiles), from x -0.9 to 0.9: perforated tiles in every other row. Two rows of twelve 42U racks (each 0.6 m wide, 1.2 m deep, 2.0 m high) face each other across it: their fronts on x -0.9 and x 0.9, from y 0 to 7.2.

Beyond the far doors: the hall's 2.4 m walkway and the hall's end wall at y 9.6, painted cobalt blue, plain, seen through the glass. A card reader and keypad on the far doors' right-hand frame at 1.1 m (x 0.95).
Above the roof: a yellow fibre tray and a black cable basket run along the aisle at 2.7 m; linear lights at 3.4 m.
The open rack: on the left row at y 3.0 to 3.6, its perforated door swung open about 180 degrees and folded back flat against the next rack's door (to y 4.2).

scenes.what: an abstract picture of the company's network as a calm, pale space: a gridded floor receding to a soft horizon, rounded plinths standing for servers, laptops, phones and a router, cobalt links lying on the floor between them, a firewall wall across one link and a cloud floating above the horizon
scenes.for: how data travels, encryption, a firewall, ransomware spreading from one laptop, phishing links leading to a server, personified threats
plan: Abstract place, no real floor plan: the composition below is written directly in frame terms (1920 by 1080, y down) and was not plan-checked with the camera tool.

The space's scale is set by the cast: a standing character is about 1.75 m, a node's plinth 1.6 m across and 0.5 m high, the symbol on it (a server, a laptop, a phone, a router) drawn large, about 1.2 m across, a firewall 2.2 m high and 3 m long, so characters can stand beside and between the objects. Frame sizes below follow one rule: at any depth, the floor's distance below the horizon equals the camera's eye height of 1.2 m.

Layout seen from above, as an idea of depth only: a laptop node near the camera at the right, a router node in the middle ground at the centre left, a server node beyond it, a phone node and two small far nodes near the horizon, the cloud floating above the far horizon at the right; links join laptop to router, router to server, router to phone and the server to the cloud; the firewall stands across the link between the router and the server.
scenes.camera: A low eye height for the cast's scale (1.2 m), looking level across the floor, so standing characters' heads rise clear of the horizon into the sky; a lens like 35 mm; one-point perspective with the horizon at y 540 (50 percent) and the vanishing point at x 960; the floor grid's lines run to that point, cross lines stay level.
scenes.composition: The pale sky fills the top half down to a soft horizon at y 540; the grid floor fills the bottom half, its lines converging to x 960, y 540. Middle ground, centre left: the router node, its plinth from about x 565 to 778 (base y 700, top y 633), the router symbol on it up to about y 570. Beyond it, slightly right: the firewall, a translucent wall from about x 912 to 1087 (foot y 610, top y 482), its gate opening near its middle where the link passes. Beyond the firewall: the server node, its plinth about x 997 to 1063 (base y 590, top y 569), the server rack on it up to about y 486. Near the camera at the right: the laptop node, its plinth from about x 1400 to 1813 (base y 850, top y 721), the large laptop symbol on it up to about y 410, its screen facing the camera and a little left. Left near the horizon: the phone node (plinth about x 310 to 370, base y 585, the phone up to about y 540). Two small far nodes on the horizon at about x 640 and 1280. The cloud floats in the sky at the upper right, far beyond the laptop and clear of it (about x 1500 to 1840, y 250 to 380). Links: from the laptop node curving left to the router (passing about x 1100, y 790), from the router through the firewall's gate to the server, from the router left to the phone, and from the server up into the cloud. Free zones for the cast (personified threats or people), each seen whole with the head against plain sky: one standing on the floor in the left foreground (feet about x 380, y 900; head top about y 375); one standing between the laptop and the router (feet about x 1180, y 860; head top about y 393), right of the firewall and well left of the cloud. Leave the band between y 600 and 760 across the middle clear of any extra objects, for packets to travel.
scenes.light: Soft, even, high light from above and slightly from the left, like an overcast studio: no sun, no glow halos, no dark areas. Each object casts a soft, short contact shadow straight down onto the floor, a little to the right. The links and the packets are the most saturated colour in the picture. Distance is shown by a gentle fade toward the horizon (haze about 0.3 at the horizon).
